conformal_instance.statement: the rescaled fixture metric is exactly Bach-flat, an instance of conformal covariance of the Bach tensor; no general transformation theorem is certified here

conventions.bach: B_ab = nabla^c nabla^d C_acbd + (1/2) R^cd C_acbd

linearized_dictionary.statement: on Minkowski TT modes these conventions reduce to B_mn = d^r d^s C_mrns

conventions.riemann: R^a_bcd = d_c Gamma^a_db - d_d Gamma^a_cb + Gamma^a_ce Gamma^e_db - Gamma^a_de Gamma^e_cb
conventions.weyl: C_abcd = R_abcd - (g_ac R_bd - g_ad R_bc + g_bd R_ac - g_bc R_ad)/2 + R (g_ac g_bd - g_ad g_bc)/6

declaration.background_family: static spherical Bach vacuum, MK chart of the Laurent constraint variety
declaration.conformal_frame: unphysical working gauge b = 1/a with areal radius; no physical matter/clock frame declared
declaration.generator: none; chart vector d_v recorded, horizon generator not yet a certified phase-space object
declaration.horizon_condition: chart-level only: simple roots of B with finite curvature invariants and EF-smooth metric
declaration.infinity_condition: none imposed; family is generically not asymptotically flat
declaration.theory: pure-Weyl gravity S_W = alpha Integral(sqrt(-g) C_abcd C^abcd)

ef_chart.chart_generator: d_v, smooth across the horizons in this chart
ef_chart.null_hypersurface_check: g^rr = B(r) exactly, so a constant-r hypersurface is null precisely at roots of B

horizon_fixture.surface_gravity_caveat: chart values kappa = B'(r_h)/2 for the chart vector d_v; the family is not asymptotically flat, so no preferred normalization of the generator is claimed

laurent_completeness.ansatz: B = w - u/r + gamma*r - k*r**2 + c2/r**2 + c3*r**3, b = 1/B
laurent_completeness.beyond_laurent_class: CLOSED by BH0B_GENERAL_STATIC_SPHERICAL_COMPLETENESS, in the conformal gauge b = 1/B and for an arbitrary C^4 nonvanishing B. The three Bach rows lie in the span of {N, r^3 B L} with L = (r B)'''' LINEAR, and both generators are recovered from the rows, so Bach = 0 <=> L = 0 and N = 0. Substituting u = r B makes L = 0 into u'''' = 0, whose solution space is exactly the cubics by four integrations -- so the Laurent form is FORCED rather than assumed, and the Groebner conditions above are recovered as a corollary. Riegert's classification is no longer the only route. Still open: the reduction of the general TWO-FUNCTION ansatz to this gauge, which is assumed.
laurent_completeness.statement: within this Laurent class Bach flatness holds iff c2 = c3 = 0 and w**2 + 3*u*gamma = 1

missing_objects: completeness of the Bach vacuum for the general TWO-FUNCTION ansatz. The conformal-gauge case is closed by BH0B_GENERAL_STATIC_SPHERICAL_COMPLETENESS; that an arbitrary diag(-a, b, r^2, ...) can be brought to b = 1/a by a conformal transformation and a radial reparametrisation is the standard Mannheim-Kazanas argument and remains assumed here.

residual_gauge.cubic: Q(x) = -u*x**3 + w*x**2 + gamma*x - k with x = 1/r
residual_gauge.dilation: beta -> beta/lambda, gamma -> lambda*gamma, k -> lambda**2*k with t -> lambda*t, r = lambda*rho, Omega = 1/lambda
residual_gauge.invariant_meaning: disc(Q) = 0 is exactly the degenerate-horizon locus, so the residual-gauge-invariant content of the family is the horizon root structure plus J
residual_gauge.singular_rescaling_caveat: Omega = 1 - c*rho vanishes at rho = 1/c; the c-map is a local gauge equivalence on rho < 1/c only and is not used to identify horizon geometries globally
residual_gauge.translation_property: the c-map acts on Q exactly as x -> x - c; the dilation as Q(x) -> lambda**2*Q(x/lambda)

singularities.classification: all listed invariants are rational in r with poles only at r = 0; WeylSq ~ 48*beta**2/r**6 gives a curvature singularity iff beta != 0; R ~ 6*beta*gamma/r**2 adds a scalar-curvature singularity iff beta*gamma != 0; every invariant is finite at every horizon
singularities.conformal_frame_note: statements are for the working gauge; WeylSq has conformal weight -4, so its zero/pole locus is frame-covariant but its value is not

vacuum_family.constraint_form: w = 1 - 3*beta*gamma, u = beta*(2 - 3*beta*gamma) parametrize the sheet of w**2 + 3*u*gamma = 1 through w = 1

dictionary.mannheim_kazanas_1989: identical (beta, gamma, k); their u = beta*(2 - 3*beta*gamma)

vacuum_family.unparametrized_sheet: the complementary sheet (e.g. w = -1, gamma = 0, B = -1 - u/r - k*r**2) has r timelike where B < 0 and is a Kantowski--Sachs-type branch outside the MK chart
